14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
27: 
28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
29: |---------------|-----------------|
30: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
31: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
32: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
33: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
34: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
69: 
70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
72: 
73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95: 
96: #### BAD Intro Structure (duplicates content)
97: 
98: ```markdown
99: # Git Commit Workflows
100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
104: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!
118: ```
119: 
120: #### Intro vs Section 1 Content Placement
121: 
122: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
123: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
124: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
125: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
126: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
127: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
128: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
129: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
130: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |
131: 
132: ---
133: 
134: ### Reference Body Skeleton
135: 
136: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.
137: 
138: ```markdown
139: # [Title]
140: 
141: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 1. OVERVIEW
146: 
147: ### Purpose
148: 
149: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
150: 
151: ### When to Use
152: 
153: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
154: - [Second trigger]
155: 
156: ### Core Principle
157: 
158: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
159: 
160: ### Boundaries
161: 
162: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
163: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
164: 
165: ### Key Sources
166: 
167: - [title](url) - [What the source establishes]
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## 2. [CONTENT SECTION]
172: 
173: ### [Rule Group]
174: 
175: - **Rule:** [What to do]
176: - **Why:** [The failure it prevents]
177: - **Check:** [How to verify it]
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## 3. [CONTENT SECTION]
182: 
183: [Body of the section]
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## 4. RELATED RESOURCES
188: 
189: - [title](./sibling-reference.md) - [What the reader gets there]
190: ```
191: 
192: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.
194: - Content sections use integer numbers only: `## 2.`, `## 3.`, and so on.
195: - Rule fields are `- **Label:** text` bullets, never two bold labels on consecutive lines.
196: - Links are `[title](url)`, never a bare URL.
197: - Every `---` has a blank line above it, so a divider never turns the line above into a setext heading.
198: - A related section, when present, is the last H2.
199:

202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.
231: 
232: ---

234: ## 3. WHEN TO CREATE REFERENCE FILES
235: 
236: ### Create Reference File When
237: 
238: **Workflow Complexity**:
239: - Multi-phase workflows with validation checkpoints
240: - Decision trees with multiple branches
241: - Pattern libraries with 5+ variations
242: - Systematic debugging procedures
243: 
244: **Technical Depth**:
245: - Root cause analysis required
246: - Tool integration details (MCP, scripts)
247: - Before/after code transformations
248: - Common error patterns and fixes
249: 
250: **Size Threshold**:
251: - Content exceeds 200 lines
252: - Multiple related workflows
253: - Extensive troubleshooting needed
254: 
255: ### Keep in SKILL.md When
256: 
257: **Core Content**:
258: - Overview and "When to Use"
259: - High-level workflow (3-5 steps)
260: - Essential rules (ALWAYS/NEVER/ESCALATE IF)

262: - Quick reference

264: **Size**: Content under 200 lines

267: 
268: | Type                | Purpose                                | Example (kebab-case)          | Size           |
269: | ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------- |

277: **Note:** All authored reference file names use kebab-case (hyphens, lowercase).

281: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
282: 
283: ### Core Principle Statements
284: 
285: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom
286: 
287: > **PLACEMENT**: Core Principle goes in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph after the H1 title.
288: 
289: **Format**:
290: ```markdown
291: \## 1. OVERVIEW
292: 
293: ### Purpose
294: 
295: [The outcome this reference produces]
296: 
297: ### When to Use
298: 
299: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
300: 
301: ### Core Principle
302: 
303: [Single powerful statement that captures the workflow's essence]
304: ```
305: 
306: **Examples from Real Skills**:
307: - "Wait for the actual condition you care about, not a guess about how long it takes"
308: - "ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure"
309: - "Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history"
310: 
311: ### Phased Workflows with Validation
312: 
313: **Purpose**: Structured processes with mandatory checkpoints
314: 
315: **Format**:
316: ```markdown
317: ### The [Number] Phases
318: 
319: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
320: 
321: #### Phase 1: [Phase Name]
322: 
323: **Purpose**: [What this phase accomplishes]
324: 
325: **Actions**:
326: 1. [Action 1]
327: 2. [Action 2]
328: 
329: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`

331: #### Phase 2: [Phase Name]
332: 
333: [Similar structure]

336: **Key Elements**:
337: - **"You MUST complete"** - Mandatory language

341: ### Before/After Code Examples
342: 
343: **Purpose**: Show transformation from wrong to right
344: 
345: **Format**:
346: ```markdown
347: ### [Pattern Name]
348:

353: \```
354:

358: // Showing correct approach
359: \```
360: 
361: **Why better**: [Explanation of improvement]
362: ```
363: 
364: **Key Elements**:
365: - `BEFORE:` marker for the wrong-way code
366: - `AFTER:` marker for the right-way code
367: - Inline comments explaining issues
368: - "Why better" rationale

381: | [Scenario 2] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |
382: ```
383: 
384: **Use when**: Multiple scenarios need comparison

386: ### Decision Logic in Markdown
387: 
388: **Purpose**: Explicit if/then logic for workflow decisions
389: 
390: **Format**:
391: \```markdown

393: 
394: \```markdown

501: \```

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766:

769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible

884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass

27: | Skill | A skill needs human-facing context beyond `SKILL.md` | This file |
28: | Feature | A user-facing feature needs setup, usage or behavior notes | This file |
29: | Component | A reusable module has an API, examples or configuration | This file, trimmed |
30: | Code Folder | A source directory needs developer orientation | [`readme-code-template.md`](./readme-code-template.md) |

32: Create a README when someone can land in the folder and need orientation. Skip it when inline comments or a nearby parent README already explain the folder.
33: 
34: ```text

36: +-- Yes: write a general README.
37: `-- No: is this source-code orientation?

50: | Section | Include When | Content |
51: |---|---|---|
52: | Overview | Always | Purpose, audience, main value and prerequisites |
53: | Key Statistics | Useful facts help readers decide scope | Counts, version, supported modes, limits |

20: ## 1. README SELECTION
21: 
22: README files answer two questions: what is this, and how does someone use or navigate it?
23: 
24: | Type | Use When | Template |
25: |---|---|---|
26: | Project | The repository or package needs a public entry point | This file |
27: | Skill | A skill needs human-facing context beyond `SKILL.md` | This file |
28: | Feature | A user-facing feature needs setup, usage or behavior notes | This file |
29: | Component | A reusable module has an API, examples or configuration | This file, trimmed |
30: | Code Folder | A source directory needs developer orientation | [`readme-code-template.md`](./readme-code-template.md) |
31: 
32: Create a README when someone can land in the folder and need orientation. Skip it when inline comments or a nearby parent README already explain the folder.

36: +-- Yes: write a general README.
37: `-- No: is this source-code orientation?

16: # Devin CLI - Complete Command Reference
17: 
18: Open this when a dispatch misbehaves or a flag's accepted value is in doubt. The tables record what the installed binary accepts, including values its help text leaves out.

20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Purpose
25: 
26: Provide a comprehensive, single-source reference for all Devin CLI commands, flags, models, configuration options, permission modes, and troubleshooting guidance.
27: 
28: ### When to Use
29: 
30: - Setting up or configuring Devin CLI
31: - Looking up command-line flags, subcommands, or permission modes
32: - Troubleshooting authentication, sandbox, or session issues
33: - Configuring subagents via `.devin/agents/[name]/AGENT.md`
34: - Selecting the right permission mode for a task
35: 
36: ### Core Principle
37: 
38: Devin CLI is Cognition's terminal-based AI coding agent — a fast, minimal agent that lives both in the terminal and in the cloud. It fronts a broad multi-model surface; this skill curates seven families in scope — DeepSeek, Gemini, GLM-5.2, GPT-5.6 (Luna Max), GPT-6 (Luna Max), Grok (4.5 and 4.6), and SWE-2 (full catalog: [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md)). Devin's native Adaptive model router and its full 48-family roster remain available via `devin models list` but are out of this skill's curated scope. The skill dispatches `swe` (alias → `swe-2`) at `accept-edits` permission mode by default; users can override the model and mode. It provides direct access to multi-model coding, subagent delegation, cloud handoff, MCP integration, and session management — all governed by configurable permission modes.
39: 
40: ### Key Sources
41: 
42: | Source | URL |
43: |--------|-----|
44: | **Documentation** | [docs.devin.ai/cli](https://docs.devin.ai/cli) |
45: | **Web App** | [app.devin.ai](https://app.devin.ai) |
46: | **Runtime** | Node.js / native binary |
47: | **Version** | 3000.2.17 |

52: 
53: | Method | Command | Notes |
54: |--------|---------|-------|
55: | **Interactive setup** | `devin setup` | Wizard for auth + MCP configuration |
56: | **Direct install** | `curl -fsSL https://devin.ai/install \| bash` | Persistent install |
57: | **Update** | `devin update` | Check for and install updates |
58: | **Force update** | `devin update --force` | Re-install even if on latest version |
59: 
60: **Platform support:**
61: 
62: | Platform | Status |
63: |----------|--------|
64: | macOS | Full support (sandbox via Seatbelt, works out of the box) |
65: | Linux | Full support (sandbox requires `bwrap` + `socat`) |
66: | Windows (WSL) | Use WSL 2; native Windows cannot run the sandbox |
67: 
68: After installation, run `devin` for the interactive REPL or `devin -p -- "prompt"` for non-interactive use.
69:

72: ## 3. AUTHENTICATION
73: 
74: cli-devin authenticates through **Devin account OAuth only** — `devin auth login` (browser flow). It does not use an API key.
75: 
76: **OAuth login/logout:**
77: 
78: ```bash
79: # Authenticate via Devin account (opens browser)
80: devin auth login
81: 
82: # For SSH/remote sessions (skip browser, manually paste token)
83: devin auth login --force-manual-token-flow
84: 
85: # View authentication status
86: devin auth status
87: 
88: # Log out and clear stored credentials
89: devin auth logout
90: ```
91:

93:

95: Logged in (via Devin).
96: 
97: Credentials:
98:   File:              ~/.local/share/devin/credentials.toml
99:   API server:        https://server.codeium.com
100:   Devin webapp:      https://app.devin.ai
101:   Devin API:         https://api.devin.ai
102: ```
103: 
104: ---
105: 
106: ## 4. COMMAND-LINE FLAGS
107: 
108: ### Essential Flags
109: 
110: | Flag | Short | Values | Description |
111: |------|-------|--------|-------------|
112: | `--model` | | `<model-name>` | Model to use — `swe` (default alias → `swe-2`), plus the curated DeepSeek / GLM-5.2 / GPT-5.6 Luna Max / GPT-6 Luna Max / Grok (4.5 and 4.6) / SWE-2 families (see §5) |
113: | `--permission-mode` | | canonical: `normal`, `accept-edits`, `smart`, `dangerous`, `autonomous` — aliases: `auto`→`normal`, `yolo`/`bypass`→`dangerous` | Permission mode controlling tool auto-approval. **`devin --help` prints only 4 of these 8 accepted values** — it is not the authoritative enum. See the probe below. |
114: | `--print` | `-p` | `[<prompt>]` | Non-interactive mode: print response and exit |
115: | `--continue` | `-c` | (none) | Continue the most recent session in the current directory |
116: | `--resume` | `-r` | `[<session-id>]` | Resume a specific session by ID, or select interactively |
117: | `--sandbox` | | (none) | Enable OS-level process sandboxing (selects `autonomous` permission mode) |
118: | `--prompt-file` | | `<file>` | Load the initial prompt from a file |
119: | `--config` | | `<path>` | Configuration file path (override default `~/.config/devin/config.json`) |
120: | `--export` | | `[<path>]` | Export conversation to a file after each turn (ATIF format) |
121: | `--agent-config` | | `<file>` | Declarative agent configuration file (JSON or YAML) |
122: | `--respect-workspace-trust` | | `true`, `false` | Respect workspace trust settings |
123: 
124: > **Verifying a flag value without spending a session.** `--help` under-reports the
125: > `--permission-mode` enum, so never conclude a value is invalid because help omits it.
126: > Force parse-time validation instead: an invalid value fails at exit 2 before the file
127: > is read, a valid one reaches the file error at exit 1.
128: >
129: > ```bash
130: > devin --permission-mode <value> --prompt-file /nonexistent
131: > #   exit 2 + "invalid value ..."        -> rejected by the binary
132: > #   exit 1 + "Failed to read prompt file" -> accepted
133: > ```
134: >

136: > `dangerous`, `yolo`, `bypass`, `autonomous` all accepted; `plan` and `manual`
137: > (Claude's modes, not Devin's) rejected. Re-run the probe after a CLI upgrade —
138: > `smart` was rejected at 3000.2.17 and is accepted at 3000.6.7.

140: ### Prompt Syntax
141: 
142: ```bash
143: # Interactive REPL (no prompt)
144: devin
145: 
146: # Start REPL with initial prompt (use -- before the prompt)
147: devin -- your prompt here
148: 
149: # Non-interactive: print mode
150: devin -p -- "prompt"
151: devin -p -- "prompt words here"    # Same, using -- separator
152: ```
153: 
154: ### Permission Mode Values
155: 
156: | Value | Behavior | Best For |
157: |-------|----------|----------|
158: | `auto` | Auto-approves read-only tools; prompts for writes and shell | Review, analysis, research |
159: | `accept-edits` | Auto-approves workspace edits + read-only; prompts for shell | Code generation, bug fixing, documentation |
160: | `smart` | Auto-runs actions a fast model judges safe | Trusted workflows with judgment calls |
161: | `dangerous` | Auto-approves all tools without prompting | Full trust — **requires explicit user approval** |
162: | `autonomous` | Sandbox-enforced; only available with `--sandbox` | Unattended execution with OS-level limits |
163:

165:

169:

172:

176: # Continue the most recent session
177: devin -c
178: 
179: # Resume a specific session
180: devin -r brisk-otter
181: 
182: # With OS-level sandbox
183: devin --sandbox -p -- "Run the test suite and fix failures"
184: 
185: # Load prompt from file
186: devin -p --prompt-file ./prompt.txt
187: 
188: # Export conversation
189: devin --export out.json -- fix the tests
190: 
191: # Start REPL with initial prompt
192: devin -- add a login page
193: ```
194: 
195: ---
196: 
197: ## 5. MODEL SELECTION
198: 
199: ### Supported Models
200: 
201: Devin dispatches **`swe`** (alias → `swe-2`) at the **`accept-edits`** permission mode by default. The model is switched per-dispatch with `--model <alias>` (short names resolve to the latest version in that family). There is no headless reasoning-effort flag — depth is expressed through the permission mode (autonomy) and the chosen model, not a reasoning flag; interactive REPL sessions cycle thinking depth with `Alt+T` (macOS: `Opt+T`).
202: 
203: **Full curated roster (DeepSeek / Gemini / GLM-5.2 / GPT-5.6 Luna Max / SWE-2 families) → [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md).** Devin's native Adaptive router and full 48-family roster are out of this skill's curated scope.
204: 
205: ### Setting the Model
206: 
207: ```bash
208: # Command flag
209: devin --model gpt-5-6-luna-max -- refactor this module
210: devin --model glm-5-2 -- explain this code
211: devin -p --model swe -- "list all TODO comments"
212: 
213: # Slash command (inside REPL)
214: /model gpt-5-6-luna-max
215: /model glm-5-2
216: /model deepseek-v4-flash-max
217: 
218: # Config file (~/.config/devin/config.json)
219: {
220:   "agent": {
221:     "model": "swe"
222:   }
223: }
224: ```
225: 
226: ### Selection Strategy
227: 
228: | Task Type | Model | Rationale |
229: |-----------|-------|-----------|
230: | Architecture decisions | `gpt-5-6-luna-max` | Multi-faceted analysis benefits from deep reasoning |
231: | Security audits | `gpt-5-6-luna-max` | Catches subtle vulnerability patterns |
232: | Complex planning | `gpt-5-6-luna-max` / `glm-5-2-max` | Multi-strategy evaluation benefits from depth |
233: | Code generation | `glm-5-2` / `glm-5-2-max` | Balanced for most generation tasks |
234: | Standard code review | `glm-5-2` / `swe-2-high` | Efficient for pattern-based review |
235: | Implementation | `glm-5-2` / `swe-2-high` | Balanced for translating specs to code |
236: | Test generation | `swe-2-high` / `glm-5-2` | Solid test structure output |
237: | Documentation | `glm-5-2` / `swe` | Efficient for structured doc generation |
238: | Quick edits / lookups | `swe-2-medium` | Lowest-effort SWE-2 tier, free |
239: | Lowest latency, cost accepted | `swe-1-7-lightning` | The only lightning tier; metered, not free |
240: | Cost-sensitive work | `swe` / `swe-2-medium` | SWE-2 is free across all three effort tiers |
241: 
242: Always specify `--model` explicitly in scripts for predictability; omitting it relies on the CLI default from `~/.config/devin/config.json`, which may differ across machines.
243: 
244: ---
245: 
246: ## 6. OUTPUT HANDLING
247: 
248: ### Print Mode Output
249: 
250: `devin -p` writes its output to stdout. Use shell redirection or command substitution to capture it.
251: 
252: ```bash
253: # Capture to file
254: devin -p \
255:   --model swe \
256:   -- \
257:   "Generate a TypeScript interface for the User model" > /tmp/user-interface.ts
258: 
259: # Capture to variable
260: RESULT=$(devin -p --model swe -- "List all exported functions in src/")
261: echo "$RESULT"
262: 
263: # Pipe to another command
264: devin -p --model swe -- "Generate SQL schema for users table" | psql -d mydb -f -
265: 
266: # Redirect stderr separately
267: devin -p --model swe -- "Analyze auth flow" > /tmp/analysis.txt 2>/tmp/errors.txt
268: ```
269: 
270: ### Export Format
271: 
272: Use `--export` to save the full conversation in ATIF format:
273: 
274: ```bash
275: # Export to default path
276: devin --export -- fix the tests
277: 
278: # Export to specific file
279: devin --export out.json -- fix tests
280: ```
281: 
282: ### Exit Codes
283: 
284: | Code | Meaning |
285: |------|---------|
286: | `0` | Success |
287: | Non-zero | Error (check stderr for details) |
288: 
289: ---
290: 
291: ## 7. INTERACTIVE COMMANDS
292: 
293: When running `devin` in interactive (REPL) mode, these slash commands are available:
294: 
295: ### Navigation & Control
296: 
297: | Command | Description |
298: |---------|-------------|
299: | `/help` | See all available commands |
300: | `/exit` or `/quit` | Exit the application |
301: | `/clear` or `/new` | Clear conversation history (start fresh) |
302: 
303: ### Mode Switching
304: 
305: | Command | Description |
306: |---------|-------------|
307: | `/mode` | Show current mode |
308: | `/mode <name>` | Switch mode (`normal`, `accept-edits`, `plan`, `bypass`; `autonomous` in sandbox sessions) |
309: | `/normal` | Switch to Normal mode (default) |
310: | `/accept-edits` | Switch to Accept Edits mode |
311: | `/plan` | Switch to Plan mode (read-only planning) |
312: | `/ask <question>` | Ask a question without making code changes (oneshot) |
313: | `/bypass` | Switch to Bypass mode (aliases: `/yolo`, `/dangerous`) |
314: 
315: ### Model Switching
316: 
317: | Command | Description |
318: |---------|-------------|
319: | `/model` | Show model selector |
320: | `/model <name>` | Switch to a specific model |
321: | `/fast` | Switch to SWE-1.6 Fast |
322: 
323: ### Session Management
324: 
325: | Command | Description |
326: |---------|-------------|
327: | `/resume` | Open the interactive session picker |
328: | `/resume <id>` | Resume session by ID |
329: | `/continue [id]` | Resume most recent or specific session |
330: | `/fork [step]` | Fork the current session to a new session |
331: | `/steps` | List conversation steps (use with `/fork` and `/revert`) |
332: | `/revert <step>` | Revert file changes from a specific step onwards |
333: | `/ls [--all]` | List recent sessions (current directory only by default) |
334: | `/rm-session <id>` | Irreversibly delete a session |
335: | `/rename-session <title>` | Rename the current session |
336: 
337: ### Cloud Sessions
338: 
339: | Command | Description |
340: |---------|-------------|
341: | `/handoff [task]` | Hand off the current session to a cloud Devin session |
342: | `/cloud-sessions [--all]` | Open interactive picker of recent cloud sessions |
343: | `/cloud-attach <id>` | Attach to a cloud Devin session with full TUI |
344: 
345: ### Workspace
346: 
347: | Command | Description |
348: |---------|-------------|
349: | `/workspace` | List workspace directories |
350: | `/add-dir <path>` | Add additional workspace directory |
351: | `/undo-add-dir <path>` | Remove a workspace directory |
352: 
353: ### Automation
354: 
355: | Command | Description |
356: |---------|-------------|
357: | `/loop <prompt>` | Run a prompt then auto-review the diff in a loop |
358: 
359: ### Utilities
360: 
361: | Command | Description |
362: |---------|-------------|
363: | `/context` | Show context window usage |
364: | `/usage` | Show estimated credit/ACU usage for the session |
365: | `/compact` | Force conversation compaction |
366: | `/login` | Authenticate with your account |
367: | `/logout` | Clear stored credentials and exit |
368: | `/update [--force]` | Check for and install updates |
369: | `/hooks` | List all loaded hooks |
370: 
371: ---
372: 
373: ## 8. SPECIAL INPUT SYNTAX
374: 
375: ### File References
376: 
377: Use `@` in the REPL to open autocomplete for local files/directories. Selected files are added as context.
378: 
379: ```bash
380: # In the REPL, type:
381: @src/utils.ts refactor this to use the repository pattern
382: ```
383: 
384: ### Image Input
385: 
386: Paste images from your clipboard with `Ctrl+V`. Attached images appear in the input area and can be managed with `Left/Right` to navigate and `Backspace` to remove.
387: 
388: ### Shell Integration
389: 
390: ```bash
391: # Pass git diff as context
392: git diff HEAD~1 | devin -p --model swe -- "Summarize these changes"
393: 
394: # Combine file content with prompt
395: cat src/auth.ts | devin -p --model swe -- "Add input validation to all functions"
396: ```
397: 
398: ---
399: 
400: ## 9. CONFIGURATION FILES
401: 
402: ### Directory Structure
403: 
404: ```
405: .devin/
406: ├── config.json          # Project-level CLI configuration
407: ├── config.local.json    # Local override (not shared with team)
408: ├── hooks/               # Lifecycle hooks
409: └── agents/
410:     └── [name]/
411:         └── AGENT.md     # Custom subagent profile
412: ```
413: 
414: ### config.json Format
415: 
416: ```json
417: // .devin/config.json or ~/.config/devin/config.json
418: {
419:   "agent": {
420:     "model": "swe"
421:   },
422:   "permissions": {
423:     "allow": [
424:       "Read(src/**)",
425:       "Write(src/**)",
426:       "Exec(git)",
427:       "Exec(npm run)"
428:     ],
429:     "deny": [
430:       "Exec(rm -rf)",
431:       "Exec(sudo)"
432:     ]
433:   },
434:   "mcpServers": {
435:     "my-server": {
436:       "command": "npx",
437:       "args": ["@company/mcp-server"],
438:       "transport": "stdio"
439:     }
440:   }
441: }
442: ```
443: 
444: ### Permission Syntax
445: 
446: **Scope-based:**
447: 
448: | Matcher | Controls | Example |
449: |---------|----------|---------|
450: | `Read(glob)` | File read access | `Read(src/**)` |
451: | `Write(glob)` | File write access | `Write(src/**)` |
452: | `Exec(prefix)` | Shell command execution | `Exec(git)`, `Exec(npm run)` |
453: | `Fetch(pattern)` | HTTP fetch access | `Fetch(https://api.github.com/*)` |
454: 
455: **Tool-based:** `read`, `edit`, `grep`, `glob`, `exec`
456: 
457: **MCP tool-based:** `mcp__server__tool`, `mcp__server__*`, `mcp__*`
458: 
459: ### Permission Precedence
460: 
461: 1. Organization/team settings (if enterprise) — highest
462: 2. Session-level grants (interactive approvals)
463: 3. Project local config (`.devin/config.local.json`)
464: 4. Project config (`.devin/config.json`)
465: 5. User config (`~/.config/devin/config.json`) — lowest
466: 
467: Deny is checked before ask, and ask is checked before allow. A deny rule always wins.
468: 
469: ---
470: 
471: ## 10. PERMISSION MODES
472: 
473: Permission modes control what the agent can do without asking for approval. Always choose the least-permissive mode that allows the task to complete.
474: 
475: ### Mode Reference
476: 
477: | Mode | Flag | Read-only | Fetch | Bash | File edits | Use Case |
478: |------|------|-----------|-------|------|------------|----------|
479: | **Auto** | `auto` | Auto | Prompt | Prompt | Prompt | Analysis, review, exploration |
480: | **Accept Edits** | `accept-edits` | Auto | Prompt | Prompt | Auto (workspace) | Code generation, refactoring |
481: | **Smart** | `smart` | Auto | Safe actions | Safe actions | Auto (workspace) | Trusted workflows with judgment |
482: | **Dangerous** | `dangerous` | Auto | Auto | Auto | Auto | Full trust — **requires explicit approval** |
483: | **Autonomous** | `autonomous` (+ `--sandbox`) | Auto | Auto (sandbox) | Auto (sandbox) | Prompt (edit/write tools bypass sandbox) | Unattended execution with OS limits |
484: 
485: ### Safety Guidance
486: 
487: ```bash
488: # SAFE: Auto mode for analysis
489: devin -p --permission-mode auto --model swe -- "Map the authentication flow"
490: 
491: # STANDARD: Accept Edits for code changes
492: devin -p --permission-mode accept-edits --model swe -- "Add error handling to all API routes"
493: 
494: # ELEVATED RISK: Dangerous mode — use only with explicit approval
495: devin -p --permission-mode dangerous --model gpt-5-6-luna-max -- "Migrate database schema"
496: 
497: # AUTONOMOUS: OS-enforced sandbox
498: devin --sandbox -p --model swe -- "Run the test suite and fix failures"
499: ```
500: 
501: ### Bypass vs Autonomous
502: 
503: | | Bypass (`dangerous`) | Autonomous (`--sandbox`) |
504: |---|---|---|
505: | Requires `--sandbox` | No | Yes (only available in sandbox sessions) |
506: | Shell commands | Auto-approved, unrestricted | Auto-approved, contained by sandbox |
507: | File writes via edit/write tools | Auto-approved anywhere | Still prompt (granting a scope expands the sandbox) |
508: | Network access | Unrestricted | Filtered by sandbox domain allow/deny lists |
509: | Respects admin Team Settings | Yes | Yes |
510: 
511: Pick `dangerous` when you trust the agent with your whole machine. Pick `--sandbox` (autonomous) when you want unattended execution with OS-enforced limits.
512: 
513: ---
514: 
515: ## 11. SESSION MANAGEMENT
516: 
517: ### Session Subcommands
518: 
519: | Subcommand | Description |
520: |------------|-------------|
521: | `devin` | Launch REPL; session picker available |
522: | `devin -c` | Continue the most recent session in the current directory |
523: | `devin -r` | Resume — pick from recent sessions interactively |
524: | `devin -r <session-id>` | Resume a specific session by ID |
525: | `devin list` | List sessions in the current directory (alias: `devin ls`) |
526: | `devin list --format json` | Output sessions as JSON |
527: | `devin list --format csv` | Output sessions as CSV |
528: 
529: ### Session Picker
530: 
531: Running `devin` without arguments opens the REPL. Use `/resume` inside the REPL to open the interactive session picker, or `/continue` to resume the most recent session.
532: 
533: ### Scripted Session Resume
534: 
535: ```bash
536: # Continue the most recent session non-interactively
537: devin -c -p "Continue implementing the rate limiter" --model swe
538: 
539: # Resume a specific session
540: devin -r brisk-otter -p "Continue from where we left off" --model swe
541: 
542: # List sessions as JSON for scripting
543: devin list --format json
544: ```
545: 
546: ### When to Use Each Operation
547: 
548: | Operation | When to Use |
549: |-----------|-------------|
550: | `-c` / `--continue` | Continue the most recent session with existing context |
551: | `-r` / `--resume` | Resume a specific session by ID |
552: | `/fork` | Fork the current session to try a different approach |
553: | `/revert` | Revert file changes from a specific step and rewind conversation |
554: | New session | Fresh context; previous session is not relevant |
555: | `-p` (stateless) | One-shot tasks; simpler to re-provide context than manage sessions |
556: 
557: ---
558: 
559: ## 12. SUBCOMMANDS
560: 
561: | Subcommand | Description |
562: |------------|-------------|
563: | `devin auth` | Authentication (login, logout, status) |
564: | `devin mcp` | MCP server management (add, list, get, remove, login, logout, enable, disable) |
565: | `devin models` | List available models organized by family |
566: | `devin rules` | Manage agent rules (always-on context blobs) |
567: | `devin skills` | Manage agent skills (slash commands and context blobs) |
568: | `devin plugins` | Manage plugins (install, list, info, update, remove) |
569: | `devin cloud` | Manage Devin Cloud resources (DRS: environment blueprints, sandbox sessions, builds) |
570: | `devin list` | List sessions in the current directory (alias: `ls`) |
571: | `devin update` | Check for and optionally install updates |
572: | `devin version` | Print the current version |
573: | `devin migrate` | Migrate configuration from other tools |
574: | `devin sandbox` | Process sandboxing for the exec tool (research preview) |
575: | `devin setup` | Interactive setup wizard |
576: | `devin uninstall` | Uninstall and remove data |
577: | `devin acp` | Run as an ACP (Agent Client Protocol) server over stdio |
578: | `devin shell` | Shell integration (init, run, setup) |
579: 
580: ---
581: 
582: ## 13. TROUBLESHOOTING
583: 
584: | Problem | Cause | Solution |
585: |---------|-------|----------|
586: | `not authenticated` / auth error | Devin account OAuth not configured | Run `devin auth login` (browser flow) |
587: | `Authentication failed` | OAuth session expired or invalid | Re-run `devin auth login` to re-authenticate |
588: | `Command not found: devin` | Not installed or not in PATH | Run `devin setup` or `curl -fsSL https://devin.ai/install \| bash`; verify with `which devin` |
589: | Task ran but no files changed | `devin -p` defaulted to `auto` (read-only) | Add `--permission-mode accept-edits` or `dangerous` |
590: | Session resume fails | Session ID invalid or expired | List sessions via `devin list`; start a new session |
591: | Slow response | Large context or complex task | Break task into smaller steps; use `auto` for analysis; use `swe-2-medium` for quick lookups, or `swe-1-7-lightning` when latency matters more than cost |
592: | `--sandbox` fails to start | Platform prerequisites missing | Run `devin sandbox setup` (Linux needs `bwrap` + `socat`; macOS works out of the box) |
593: | Cloud handoff fails | Network issue or uncommitted changes blocking | Commit or stash unwanted changes; verify connectivity to `app.devin.ai` |
594: | Subagent denied tools | Background subagent cannot prompt for permissions | Resume the subagent in the foreground to approve tools |
595: | MCP server not responding | Server not running or misconfigured | Check `devin mcp list`; verify server config in `.devin/config.json` |
596: | Windows compatibility | WSL not configured | Use WSL 2; native Windows cannot run the sandbox |
597: 
598: ---
599: 
600: ## 14. ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
601: 
602: | Variable | Purpose | Example |
603: |----------|---------|---------|
604: | `DEVIN_MODEL` | Default model override | `swe`, `glm-5-2`, `gpt-5-6-luna-max` |
605: | `DEVIN_PERMISSION_MODE` | Default permission mode | `auto`, `accept-edits`, `smart`, `dangerous` |
606: | `DEVIN_SANDBOX` | Enable sandbox | `1` |
607: | `DEVIN_PROJECT_DIR` | Project root directory (set automatically by Devin on session start) | `/path/to/project` |
608: | `WINDSURF_API_KEY` | ACP server credentials (alternative to stored auth) | API key string |

16: # Devin CLI - Complete Command Reference
17: 
18: Open this when a dispatch misbehaves or a flag's accepted value is in doubt. The tables record what the installed binary accepts, including values its help text leaves out.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Purpose
25: 
26: Provide a comprehensive, single-source reference for all Devin CLI commands, flags, models, configuration options, permission modes, and troubleshooting guidance.
27: 
28: ### When to Use
29: 
30: - Setting up or configuring Devin CLI
31: - Looking up command-line flags, subcommands, or permission modes
32: - Troubleshooting authentication, sandbox, or session issues
33: - Configuring subagents via `.devin/agents/[name]/AGENT.md`
34: - Selecting the right permission mode for a task
35: 
36: ### Core Principle
37: 
38: Devin CLI is Cognition's terminal-based AI coding agent — a fast, minimal agent that lives both in the terminal and in the cloud. It fronts a broad multi-model surface; this skill curates seven families in scope — DeepSeek, Gemini, GLM-5.2, GPT-5.6 (Luna Max), GPT-6 (Luna Max), Grok (4.5 and 4.6), and SWE-2 (full catalog: [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md)). Devin's native Adaptive model router and its full 48-family roster remain available via `devin models list` but are out of this skill's curated scope. The skill dispatches `swe` (alias → `swe-2`) at `accept-edits` permission mode by default; users can override the model and mode. It provides direct access to multi-model coding, subagent delegation, cloud handoff, MCP integration, and session management — all governed by configurable permission modes.
39: 
40: ### Key Sources
41: 
42: | Source | URL |
43: |--------|-----|
44: | **Documentation** | [docs.devin.ai/cli](https://docs.devin.ai/cli) |
45: | **Web App** | [app.devin.ai](https://app.devin.ai) |
46: | **Runtime** | Node.js / native binary |
47: | **Version** | 3000.2.17 |
48: 
49: ---
50: 
51: ## 2. INSTALLATION
52: 
53: | Method | Command | Notes |
54: |--------|---------|-------|
55: | **Interactive setup** | `devin setup` | Wizard for auth + MCP configuration |
56: | **Direct install** | `curl -fsSL https://devin.ai/install \| bash` | Persistent install |
57: | **Update** | `devin update` | Check for and install updates |
58: | **Force update** | `devin update --force` | Re-install even if on latest version |
59: 
60: **Platform support:**
61: 
62: | Platform | Status |
63: |----------|--------|
64: | macOS | Full support (sandbox via Seatbelt, works out of the box) |
65: | Linux | Full support (sandbox requires `bwrap` + `socat`) |
66: | Windows (WSL) | Use WSL 2; native Windows cannot run the sandbox |
67: 
68: After installation, run `devin` for the interactive REPL or `devin -p -- "prompt"` for non-interactive use.
69: 
70: ---
71: 
72: ## 3. AUTHENTICATION
73: 
74: cli-devin authenticates through **Devin account OAuth only** — `devin auth login` (browser flow). It does not use an API key.
75: 
76: **OAuth login/logout:**
77: 
78: ```bash
79: # Authenticate via Devin account (opens browser)
80: devin auth login
81: 
82: # For SSH/remote sessions (skip browser, manually paste token)
83: devin auth login --force-manual-token-flow
84: 
85: # View authentication status
86: devin auth status
87: 
88: # Log out and clear stored credentials
89: devin auth logout
90: ```
91: 
92: **Auth status output:**
93: 
94: ```
95: Logged in (via Devin).
96: 
97: Credentials:
98:   File:              ~/.local/share/devin/credentials.toml
99:   API server:        https://server.codeium.com
100:   Devin webapp:      https://app.devin.ai
101:   Devin API:         https://api.devin.ai
102: ```
103: 
104: ---
105: 
106: ## 4. COMMAND-LINE FLAGS
107: 
108: ### Essential Flags
109: 
110: | Flag | Short | Values | Description |
111: |------|-------|--------|-------------|
112: | `--model` | | `<model-name>` | Model to use — `swe` (default alias → `swe-2`), plus the curated DeepSeek / GLM-5.2 / GPT-5.6 Luna Max / GPT-6 Luna Max / Grok (4.5 and 4.6) / SWE-2 families (see §5) |
113: | `--permission-mode` | | canonical: `normal`, `accept-edits`, `smart`, `dangerous`, `autonomous` — aliases: `auto`→`normal`, `yolo`/`bypass`→`dangerous` | Permission mode controlling tool auto-approval. **`devin --help` prints only 4 of these 8 accepted values** — it is not the authoritative enum. See the probe below. |
114: | `--print` | `-p` | `[<prompt>]` | Non-interactive mode: print response and exit |
115: | `--continue` | `-c` | (none) | Continue the most recent session in the current directory |
116: | `--resume` | `-r` | `[<session-id>]` | Resume a specific session by ID, or select interactively |
117: | `--sandbox` | | (none) | Enable OS-level process sandboxing (selects `autonomous` permission mode) |
118: | `--prompt-file` | | `<file>` | Load the initial prompt from a file |
119: | `--config` | | `<path>` | Configuration file path (override default `~/.config/devin/config.json`) |
120: | `--export` | | `[<path>]` | Export conversation to a file after each turn (ATIF format) |
121: | `--agent-config` | | `<file>` | Declarative agent configuration file (JSON or YAML) |

197: ## 5. MODEL SELECTION
198: 
199: ### Supported Models
200: 
201: Devin dispatches **`swe`** (alias → `swe-2`) at the **`accept-edits`** permission mode by default. The model is switched per-dispatch with `--model <alias>` (short names resolve to the latest version in that family). There is no headless reasoning-effort flag — depth is expressed through the permission mode (autonomy) and the chosen model, not a reasoning flag; interactive REPL sessions cycle thinking depth with `Alt+T` (macOS: `Opt+T`).
202: 
203: **Full curated roster (DeepSeek / Gemini / GLM-5.2 / GPT-5.6 Luna Max / SWE-2 families) → [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md).** Devin's native Adaptive router and full 48-family roster are out of this skill's curated scope.

205: ### Setting the Model
206: 
207: ```bash
208: # Command flag
209: devin --model gpt-5-6-luna-max -- refactor this module
210: devin --model glm-5-2 -- explain this code
211: devin -p --model swe -- "list all TODO comments"
212: 
213: # Slash command (inside REPL)
214: /model gpt-5-6-luna-max
215: /model glm-5-2
216: /model deepseek-v4-flash-max
217:

220:   "agent": {

222:   }
223: }

227: 
228: | Task Type | Model | Rationale |
229: |-----------|-------|-----------|
230: | Architecture decisions | `gpt-5-6-luna-max` | Multi-faceted analysis benefits from deep reasoning |
231: | Security audits | `gpt-5-6-luna-max` | Catches subtle vulnerability patterns |
232: | Complex planning | `gpt-5-6-luna-max` / `glm-5-2-max` | Multi-strategy evaluation benefits from depth |
233: | Code generation | `glm-5-2` / `glm-5-2-max` | Balanced for most generation tasks |
234: | Standard code review | `glm-5-2` / `swe-2-high` | Efficient for pattern-based review |
235: | Implementation | `glm-5-2` / `swe-2-high` | Balanced for translating specs to code |
236: | Test generation | `swe-2-high` / `glm-5-2` | Solid test structure output |
237: | Documentation | `glm-5-2` / `swe` | Efficient for structured doc generation |
238: | Quick edits / lookups | `swe-2-medium` | Lowest-effort SWE-2 tier, free |
239: | Lowest latency, cost accepted | `swe-1-7-lightning` | The only lightning tier; metered, not free |

400: ## 9. CONFIGURATION FILES
401: 
402: ### Directory Structure
403: 
404: ```
405: .devin/
406: ├── config.json          # Project-level CLI configuration
407: ├── config.local.json    # Local override (not shared with team)

414: ### config.json Format
415: 
416: ```json
417: // .devin/config.json or ~/.config/devin/config.json
418: {
419:   "agent": {
420:     "model": "swe"
421:   },
422:   "permissions": {
423:     "allow": [
424:       "Read(src/**)",
425:       "Write(src/**)",
426:       "Exec(git)",
427:       "Exec(npm run)"
428:     ],
429:     "deny": [
430:       "Exec(rm -rf)",
431:       "Exec(sudo)"
432:     ]
433:   },
434:   "mcpServers": {
435:     "my-server": {
436:       "command": "npx",
437:       "args": ["@company/mcp-server"],
438:       "transport": "stdio"
439:     }
440:   }
441: }
442: ```
443: 
444: ### Permission Syntax
445: 
446: **Scope-based:**
447: 
448: | Matcher | Controls | Example |
449: |---------|----------|---------|
450: | `Read(glob)` | File read access | `Read(src/**)` |
451: | `Write(glob)` | File write access | `Write(src/**)` |
452: | `Exec(prefix)` | Shell command execution | `Exec(git)`, `Exec(npm run)` |
453: | `Fetch(pattern)` | HTTP fetch access | `Fetch(https://api.github.com/*)` |
454: 
455: **Tool-based:** `read`, `edit`, `grep`, `glob`, `exec`
456: 
457: **MCP tool-based:** `mcp__server__tool`, `mcp__server__*`, `mcp__*`
458: 
459: ### Permission Precedence
460: 
461: 1. Organization/team settings (if enterprise) — highest
462: 2. Session-level grants (interactive approvals)
463: 3. Project local config (`.devin/config.local.json`)
464: 4. Project config (`.devin/config.json`)
465: 5. User config (`~/.config/devin/config.json`) — lowest
466: 
467: Deny is checked before ask, and ask is checked before allow. A deny rule always wins.

471: ## 10. PERMISSION MODES
472: 
473: Permission modes control what the agent can do without asking for approval. Always choose the least-permissive mode that allows the task to complete.
474: 
475: ### Mode Reference
476: 
477: | Mode | Flag | Read-only | Fetch | Bash | File edits | Use Case |
478: |------|------|-----------|-------|------|------------|----------|
479: | **Auto** | `auto` | Auto | Prompt | Prompt | Prompt | Analysis, review, exploration |
480: | **Accept Edits** | `accept-edits` | Auto | Prompt | Prompt | Auto (workspace) | Code generation, refactoring |
481: | **Smart** | `smart` | Auto | Safe actions | Safe actions | Auto (workspace) | Trusted workflows with judgment |
482: | **Dangerous** | `dangerous` | Auto | Auto | Auto | Auto | Full trust — **requires explicit approval** |
483: | **Autonomous** | `autonomous` (+ `--sandbox`) | Auto | Auto (sandbox) | Auto (sandbox) | Prompt (edit/write tools bypass sandbox) | Unattended execution with OS limits |
484: 
485: ### Safety Guidance
486: 
487: ```bash
488: # SAFE: Auto mode for analysis
489: devin -p --permission-mode auto --model swe -- "Map the authentication flow"
490: 
491: # STANDARD: Accept Edits for code changes
492: devin -p --permission-mode accept-edits --model swe -- "Add error handling to all API routes"
493: 
494: # ELEVATED RISK: Dangerous mode — use only with explicit approval
495: devin -p --permission-mode dangerous --model gpt-5-6-luna-max -- "Migrate database schema"
496: 
497: # AUTONOMOUS: OS-enforced sandbox
498: devin --sandbox -p --model swe -- "Run the test suite and fix failures"
499: ```
500: 
501: ### Bypass vs Autonomous
502: 
503: | | Bypass (`dangerous`) | Autonomous (`--sandbox`) |
504: |---|---|---|
505: | Requires `--sandbox` | No | Yes (only available in sandbox sessions) |
506: | Shell commands | Auto-approved, unrestricted | Auto-approved, contained by sandbox |
507: | File writes via edit/write tools | Auto-approved anywhere | Still prompt (granting a scope expands the sandbox) |
508: | Network access | Unrestricted | Filtered by sandbox domain allow/deny lists |
509: | Respects admin Team Settings | Yes | Yes |
510: 
511: Pick `dangerous` when you trust the agent with your whole machine. Pick `--sandbox` (autonomous) when you want unattended execution with OS-enforced limits.

582: ## 13. TROUBLESHOOTING
583: 
584: | Problem | Cause | Solution |
585: |---------|-------|----------|
586: | `not authenticated` / auth error | Devin account OAuth not configured | Run `devin auth login` (browser flow) |
587: | `Authentication failed` | OAuth session expired or invalid | Re-run `devin auth login` to re-authenticate |
588: | `Command not found: devin` | Not installed or not in PATH | Run `devin setup` or `curl -fsSL https://devin.ai/install \| bash`; verify with `which devin` |
589: | Task ran but no files changed | `devin -p` defaulted to `auto` (read-only) | Add `--permission-mode accept-edits` or `dangerous` |
590: | Session resume fails | Session ID invalid or expired | List sessions via `devin list`; start a new session |
591: | Slow response | Large context or complex task | Break task into smaller steps; use `auto` for analysis; use `swe-2-medium` for quick lookups, or `swe-1-7-lightning` when latency matters more than cost |
592: | `--sandbox` fails to start | Platform prerequisites missing | Run `devin sandbox setup` (Linux needs `bwrap` + `socat`; macOS works out of the box) |
593: | Cloud handoff fails | Network issue or uncommitted changes blocking | Commit or stash unwanted changes; verify connectivity to `app.devin.ai` |
594: | Subagent denied tools | Background subagent cannot prompt for permissions | Resume the subagent in the foreground to approve tools |
595: | MCP server not responding | Server not running or misconfigured | Check `devin mcp list`; verify server config in `.devin/config.json` |
596: | Windows compatibility | WSL not configured | Use WSL 2; native Windows cannot run the sandbox |

427:

430: ### Deep Reasoning (architecture, security, planning)
431: 
432: ```bash
433: # Architecture analysis with Opus
434: devin -p "Analyze the architecture of this project. Identify coupling issues, circular dependencies, and scalability concerns." \
435:   --model opus --permission-mode auto
436: 
437: # Security audit with Opus
438: devin -p "Perform a thorough security audit of [file-path]. Check OWASP Top 10, auth bypasses, injection vectors, and cryptographic weaknesses." \
439:   --model opus --permission-mode auto
440: ```

442: ### Quick Edits (cost-sensitive)
443: 
444: ```bash
445: # Quick fix with SWE Fast
446: devin -p "Fix the typo in the error message at line 42 in [file-path]." \
447:   --model swe-1-6-fast --permission-mode accept-edits
448: 
449: # Quick lookup with SWE
450: devin -p "List all TODO comments in src/." \
451:   --model swe --permission-mode auto
452: ```

455:

457:

461:   --model opus --permission-mode auto > /tmp/security-findings.txt

471: 
472: ### Purpose
473: 
474: Append this epilogue to any delegated prompt when the calling AI needs structured session memory back from Devin CLI. The agent will include the delimited section in its output, enabling the calling AI to extract, parse, and save it via `generate-context.js`.
475: 
476: ### Epilogue Template
477: 
478: Append the following text to the end of any Devin CLI prompt:
479: 
480: ```text
481: When you finish, include a session memory section in your output using EXACTLY this format:
482: 
483: <!-- MEMORY_HANDBACK_START -->
484: ## Session Memory
485: 
486: ### Summary
487: [1-3 sentences: what was accomplished]
488: 
489: ### Files Modified
490: - path/to/file.ts
491: 
492: ### Decisions
493: - Decision and rationale
494: 
495: ### Next Steps
496: - Remaining work
497: 
498: ### Spec Folder
499: [spec-folder-name]
500: <!-- MEMORY_HANDBACK_END -->
501: ```
502: 
503: ### Extraction by Calling AI
504: 
505: After receiving agent output, the calling AI extracts the handback section:
506: 
507: ```javascript
508: const match = output.match(/<!-- MEMORY_HANDBACK_START -->([\s\S]*?)<!-- MEMORY_HANDBACK_END -->/);
509: ```
510: 
511: Then constructs structured JSON and saves via:
512: 
513: ```bash
514: # Redact or scrub secrets before writing the JSON payload
515: # Write extracted data to JSON
516: cat > /tmp/save-context-data.json << 'JSONEOF'
517: {
518:   "specFolder": "<extracted or provided by calling AI>",
519:   "user_prompts": [
520:     "<delegated task or user goal>"
521:   ],
522:   "observations": [
523:     {
524:       "type": "implementation",
525:       "title": "<short accomplishment>",
526:       "narrative": "<what changed and why it matters>",
527:       "facts": [
528:         "<verification or durable implementation detail>"
529:       ]
530:     }
531:   ],
532:   "recent_context": [
533:     {
534:       "request": "<delegated task or user goal>",
535:       "learning": "<durable implementation detail or verification result>"
536:     }
537:   ],
538:   "FILES": [
539:     {
540:       "FILE_PATH": "<extracted path when known>",
541:       "DESCRIPTION": "<what changed and why it matters>",
542:       "ACTION": "Modified",
543:       "MODIFICATION_MAGNITUDE": "small",
544:       "_provenance": "tool"
545:     }
546:   ],
547:   "sessionSummary": "<extracted summary>",
548:   "keyDecisions": ["<extracted decisions>"],
549:   "nextSteps": ["<extracted remaining work>"],
550:   "triggerPhrases": ["<auto-derived from task>"]
551: }
552: JSONEOF
553: 
554: # Save via generate-context.js JSON mode
555: node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js /tmp/save-context-data.json [spec-folder]
556: ```
557: 
558: Structured JSON is the required save path. You can pass the payload via temp file, `--stdin`, or `--json`. Do not call `generate-context.js` with only a spec folder.

472: ### Purpose

501: ```

504: 
505: After receiving agent output, the calling AI extracts the handback section:
506:

512:

515: # Write extracted data to JSON
516: cat > /tmp/save-context-data.json << 'JSONEOF'

518:   "specFolder": "<extracted or provided by calling AI>",
519:   "user_prompts": [
520:     "<delegated task or user goal>"
521:   ],
522:   "observations": [
523:     {
524:       "type": "implementation",
525:       "title": "<short accomplishment>",
526:       "narrative": "<what changed and why it matters>",
527:       "facts": [
528:         "<verification or durable implementation detail>"
529:       ]
530:     }
531:   ],
532:   "recent_context": [

536:     }
537:   ],

540:       "FILE_PATH": "<extracted path when known>",
541:       "DESCRIPTION": "<what changed and why it matters>",
542:       "ACTION": "Modified",
543:       "MODIFICATION_MAGNITUDE": "small",

16: # Devin Subagent Delegation Reference
17: 
18: Routing reference for delegating tasks to Devin CLI's subagent system.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Purpose
25: 
26: Documents Devin's subagent system and how any AI assistant orchestrates it. The calling AI acts as the **conductor** (planner, validator, integrator) while Devin CLI executes targeted tasks through its subagent profiles.
27: 
28: ### When to Use
29: 
30: - Delegating supplementary implementation or analysis tasks to Devin CLI subagents
31: - Parallel task processing through background subagents
32: - Read-only codebase exploration via `subagent_explore` (runs on cheap SWE-1.6)
33: - Code changes via `subagent_general` (runs on parent's model)
34: - Custom specialized workers defined in `.devin/agents/[name]/AGENT.md`
35: - Fresh-perspective debugging after the calling AI's attempts fail
36: 
37: ### Core Principle
38: 
39: The calling AI decides WHAT to do, Devin CLI decides HOW to do it within the delegated scope. Devin's `run_subagent` tool spawns independent workers that share tools and codebase context with the parent but operate in their own conversation chain — they do not inherit the parent's conversation history.
40: 
41: ---
42: 
43: ## 2. ORCHESTRATION MODEL
44: 
45: ```
46: Calling AI (CONDUCTOR)
47:   |
48:   |-- Analyzes task, selects subagent profile
49:   |-- Constructs devin CLI command with model + permission mode
50:   |-- Delegates via Bash tool
51:   |
52:   v
53: Devin CLI (EXECUTOR)
54:   |
55:   |-- Parent agent receives the prompt
56:   |-- Spawns subagent via run_subagent tool with selected profile
57:   |-- Subagent runs in foreground (parent pauses) or background (parallel)
58:   |-- Subagent returns result to parent, parent summarizes to caller
59:   |
60:   v
61: Calling AI (CONDUCTOR)
62:   |
63:   |-- Validates output quality
64:   |-- Integrates into workflow
65:   |-- Decides next step
66: ```
67: 
68: ### Invocation Pattern
69: 
70: Devin CLI tasks are routed through the parent agent, which spawns subagents using the `run_subagent` tool. The calling AI requests a specific profile in natural language; Devin's agent selects the appropriate profile and spawn mode.

421: 
422: ### Skills and Rules Discovery
423: 
424: The installed Devin CLI discovers repository skills and rules that are already present; cli-devin adds no adapter for either mechanism. On Devin `3000.2.17`, the live `devin skills list` output included these repo-local packets:
425: 
426: ```text
427:   /sk-doc [user,model] (./.skilled/skills/sk-doc)
428:   /cli-external-orchestration [user,model] (./.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration)
429:   /sk-git [user,model] (./.skilled/skills/sk-git)

431:   /mcp-code-mode [user,model] (./.skilled/skills/mcp-code-mode)
432:   /system-skill-advisor [user,model] (./.skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor)
433:   /system-spec-kit [user,model] (./.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit)
434:   /sk-code [user,model] (./.skilled/skills/sk-code)
435:   /system-deep-loop [user,model] (./.skilled/skills/system-deep-loop)
436:   /sk-prompt [user,model] (./.skilled/skills/sk-prompt)
437:   /sk-design-md-generator [user,model] (./.skilled/skills/sk-design/sk-design-md-generator)
438: ```
439: 
440: The live context records Devin as discovering 13 top-level skill packets. The rerun in this checkout printed the 12 concrete `./.skilled/skills/*` paths above, plus the external `devin-cli` packet and the empty-path `declarative-repo-setup` entry; the output is preserved here rather than inventing a filesystem path for the thirteenth local packet.
441: 
442: The live `devin rules list` output was:
443: 
444: ```text
445: Available Rules
446: 
447:   global_rules [Windsurf] always-on
448:   CLAUDE [Claude] always-on
449:   AGENTS [Standard] always-on
450:   CLAUDE [Claude] always-on
451: ```
452: 
453: That listing predates `.devin/config.json`, which turns Devin's Claude import off. The command still names `CLAUDE`, but a session no longer loads it: it loads the checkout's own root `AGENTS.md`, cut at Devin's fixed 16,384-byte limit per rule file. `.devin/SYNC.md` §5 records why the import is off.
454: 
455: ### Installed-Version Import Correction
456: 
457: Devin's docs claim that `.claude/agents/*.md` files are automatically imported. A live probe against the installed Devin `3000.2.17` found the repo's 13-file `.claude/agents/` directory but reported that none of those profiles were usable through `run_subagent`; only `subagent_explore` and `subagent_general` were dispatchable. This is a confirmed installed-version finding, not an assumption. A native `.devin/agents/[name]/AGENT.md` profile is required for a custom profile here. The older import note in the reference material must not be treated as working behavior for this version.
458: 
459: ### Devin Has No Command-File System
460: 
461: Commands are not a missing Devin parity feature. The installed `devin --help` lists `auth`, `mcp`, `models`, `rules`, `skills`, `plugins`, `cloud`, `list`, `update`, `version`, `migrate`, `sandbox`, `setup`, `uninstall`, `acp`, `shell`, and `help`; it has no `commands` subcommand. A direct `devin commands` probe returns `error: unexpected argument 'commands' found`, and the installed docs expose no command-file directory. This is an architectural non-concept for Devin, not a build gap.

17: # Devin CLI Built-in Tools Reference
18: 
19: Reference for all Devin CLI capabilities, highlighting unique features and the 4-tier permission model.
20: 
21: ---
22: 
23: ## 1. OVERVIEW
24: 
25: ### Purpose
26: 
27: Covers all built-in capabilities available in Devin CLI, highlights what is unique compared to other CLI executors, and provides the 4-tier permission model for task routing decisions.
28: 
29: ### When to Use
30: 
31: - Choosing whether to delegate a task to Devin CLI or handle it in the calling AI
32: - Understanding which Devin tools and permission modes to use for different task types
33: - Mapping calling AI capabilities to Devin CLI equivalents
34: - Leveraging Devin-exclusive features (subagents, /handoff, multi-model, sandbox)
35: 
36: ### Core Principle
37: 
38: Delegate to Devin CLI for capabilities the calling AI lacks natively — especially `run_subagent` for parallel subagent delegation, `/handoff` for cloud session transfer, multi-model selection, and the OS-level sandbox for autonomous execution.
39: 
40: ---
41: 
42: ## 2. UNIQUE CAPABILITIES
43: 
44: These capabilities are exclusive to Devin CLI or provide significantly different workflows.
45: 
46: ### run_subagent Tool
47: 
48: **Native subagent spawning for parallel work.** Devin's `run_subagent` tool lets the parent agent spawn independent workers that share tools and codebase context but operate in their own conversation chain.
49: 
50: **Capabilities:**
51: - Two built-in profiles: `subagent_explore` (read-only, cheap SWE-1.6) and `subagent_general` (full access, parent's model)
52: - Custom profiles via `.devin/agents/[name]/AGENT.md` with model overrides and tool restrictions
53: - Foreground (parent pauses) or background (parallel) execution
54: - Background subagents auto-deny unapproved tools; foreground subagents prompt for approval
55: - Subagents can be resumed in the foreground if they fail due to denied tools
56: 
57: **Usage:**
58: 
59: ```bash
60: # Request an explore subagent for read-only research
61: devin -p "Research the auth module using a subagent_explore subagent" \
62:   --model adaptive --permission-mode auto
63: 
64: # Request a general subagent for code changes
65: devin -p "Fix the failing tests using a subagent_general subagent" \
66:   --model adaptive --permission-mode accept-edits
67: ```
68: 
69: **Best For:**
70: - Parallel research across multiple modules
71: - Cost-effective exploration (explore subagent runs on SWE-1.6)
72: - Specialized workers via custom AGENT.md profiles
73: - Isolating subtask context from the parent conversation
74: 
75: **Compared to other CLI executors:** Most CLI executors lack native subagent spawning. Devin's `run_subagent` is a first-class tool that the agent calls automatically when a task benefits from independent work.
76: 
77: Full subagent details: [agent-delegation.md](./agent-delegation.md)
78:

16: # Cross-AI Orchestration Patterns: Calling AI + Devin CLI
17: 
18: Proven patterns for orchestrating Devin CLI from any AI assistant session.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Purpose
25: 
26: Each pattern documented here includes the rationale, implementation template, and practical considerations for combining the calling AI with Devin CLI effectively. Devin is the 5th executor kind in the cli-* family alongside cli-codex (OpenAI), cli-claude-code (Anthropic), cli-opencode (OpenCode), and cli-cursor (Cursor).
27: 
28: ### When to Use
29: 
30: - You need a second AI perspective on generated code, architecture, or security
31: - Devin's strengths (multi-model selection, subagent delegation, cloud handoff, Adaptive routing) complement the calling AI's strengths
32: - You want to run parallel AI tasks through subagents while the calling AI continues working
33: - Complex workflows benefit from structured, multi-stage generation and validation
34: - You need to offload long-running tasks to a cloud VM with browser and shell access
35: - You want cross-AI validation from a Cognition-backed model
36: 
37: ### Core Principle
38: 
39: The calling AI acts as the orchestrator (planner, validator, integrator) while Devin CLI executes targeted tasks. The value comes from combining different model perspectives and leveraging Devin's multi-model surface, subagent delegation, and cloud handoff — not from redundant work.
40: 
41: ---
42: 
43: ## 2. GENERATE-REVIEW-FIX CYCLE
44: 
45: **The most reliable cross-AI pattern.** One AI generates, the other reviews, then the original fixes.
46: 
47: ### Flow
48: 
49: ```
50: Calling AI (plan) --> Devin CLI (generate) --> Calling AI (review) --> Devin CLI (fix)
51: ```
52: 
53: ### Implementation
54: 
55: ```bash
56: # Step 1: Devin generates the code
57: devin -p \
58:   "Create a rate limiter middleware for Express with sliding window algorithm. Output only the code, no explanation." \
59:   --model adaptive --permission-mode accept-edits > /tmp/rate-limiter.ts
60: 
61: # Step 2: Calling AI reviews (done within the calling AI session)
62: # Read /tmp/rate-limiter.ts, identify issues, write review to /tmp/review.md
63: 
64: # Step 3: Devin fixes based on review
65: devin -p \
66:   "@/tmp/rate-limiter.ts Fix these issues: $(cat /tmp/review.md)" \
67:   --model adaptive --permission-mode accept-edits > /tmp/rate-limiter-v2.ts
68: ```
69: 
70: ### When to Use
71: 
72: - Code generation tasks where a second perspective catches edge cases
73: - Complex algorithms where verification matters more than speed
74: - Architecture decisions that benefit from adversarial review
75: 
76: ### Considerations
77: 
78: - Always validate the final output yourself (neither AI is infallible)
79: - Keep the review focused: bullet points of specific issues, not general feedback
80: - Limit to 2 fix cycles maximum; diminishing returns beyond that

194: ### Silent Stdin Consumption When Dispatching in a `while read` Loop
195: 
196: When a dispatcher script iterates over lines of input with `while IFS= read -r line; do ... done < input.jsonl` and launches `devin -p ... &` inside the loop body, **devin silently consumes the loop's stdin**. The loop exits after the first 3-6 iterations with no error, dropping most dispatches.
197: 
198: **Symptom:** You dispatch a 27-finding batch; only 3-6 devin processes actually launch. No error, no warning.
199: 
200: **Root cause:** `devin -p` inherits the script's stdin by default. Each backgrounded devin process reads from the same file descriptor and races with the `read` command for lines.
201: 
202: **Always pair `devin -p ... &` inside a read-loop with `</dev/null` on the redirection.**
203: 
204: ```bash
205: # BAD: devin inherits the loop's stdin, drains input.jsonl after iteration ~3
206: while IFS= read -r line; do
207:   devin -p "$PROMPT" > "$LOG" 2>&1 &
208:   echo "$!" > "pid-$LINE_ID.pid"
209: done < input.jsonl
210: 
211: # GOOD: redirect devin stdin from /dev/null so the loop keeps its own
212: while IFS= read -r line; do
213:   devin -p "$PROMPT" > "$LOG" 2>&1 </dev/null &
214:   echo "$!" > "pid-$LINE_ID.pid"
215: done < input.jsonl
216: ```
